standard.title: Create spoken, written and multimodal texts
standard.description: with support, create spoken, written and multimodal texts, using familiar words, modelled phrases and sentences, copying known characters and writing system conventions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can interact in classroom routines, collaborate in play-based activities, and locate information in familiar texts (AC9LCH2C01–C03). They can use formulaic expressions and communicate personal meaning. They have not yet created their own texts — combining target language words, phrases and writing with images and multimodal elements — for a defined purpose and audience.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students create spoken, written and multimodal texts using familiar words, modelled phrases and sentences, combining target language with images and other modes to communicate meaning for a purpose.

nodes.label: Copying and producing written target language
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can copy and produce written target language words and phrases with attention to writing conventions, using known characters or script features.
nodes.minimum_width: Copy at least five target language words or a short phrase with attention to script conventions (stroke order, character formation, or script-specific features as applicable), demonstrating understanding of what the words mean.
nodes.typical_width: Copy and trace words and phrases with attention to writing conventions; make and form characters or script features using varied materials; connect written forms to their spoken equivalents and meanings; begin to write short known phrases from memory.
wider: Explore the relationship between the written form and meaning in the target language writing system — for example, how components or character elements contribute to meaning
Compare writing conventions in the target language with English — identify what is similar and what requires different knowledge or attention
nodes.hinge_reason: Producing written target language is the prerequisite for all text creation. Students who cannot form written words with attention to script conventions cannot create written or multimodal texts — the core demand of this descriptor.

response_modes.reason: Writing script conventions require repeated practice for accuracy and fluency. Varied production activities — chalk, sand, whiteboards, digital tools — build the muscle memory and visual attention needed before students can write with confidence in text creation tasks.

success_criteria: Copies at least five target language words with correct script conventions
Can produce at least two words from memory with recognisable accuracy

nodes.label: Creating short texts for a purpose
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create short spoken, written or multimodal texts using familiar words and modelled sentence structures, for a specific purpose and audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Create at least one short text (caption, card, poster, label) using at least three target language words or a modelled phrase, with a clear communicative purpose.
nodes.typical_width: Create a range of short texts — captions for photo displays, greeting cards, posters, illustrated sentences, self-portraits with labels — using familiar words and modelled sentence structures; combine target language with images and other modes; present personal knowledge about places, people or experiences.
wider: Create a bilingual text that communicates the same information in both the target language and English — compare the choices made and what is easier or harder to express in each language
Create a text for a specific audience (younger students, family, community) and adapt the language choices accordingly

response_modes.reason: Text creation for a purpose requires students to understand that different purposes and audiences call for different language choices. Varied creation tasks — personal, informative, celebratory — build this contextual awareness before students can make independent text choices.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Background learners have authentic content to communicate — family stories, cultural knowledge, places of personal significance. Width investment in creation tasks that draw on this personal content produces genuinely communicative texts rather than exercises, and builds the connection between target language and personal identity.
success_criteria: Creates a short text using at least three target language words or a modelled phrase
The text has a clear communicative purpose and is directed at an identifiable audience

nodes.label: Performing and presenting created texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can perform or present a created spoken or multimodal text — a role-play, short play, or oral presentation — using the target language with support.
nodes.minimum_width: Perform or present at least one created text (role-play script, short play, oral presentation) using at least four target language phrases appropriate to the context.
nodes.typical_width: Role-play modelled conversations incorporating personal information; perform short plays based on familiar stories using puppets and props; practise and present oral texts using toys, costumes or visual supports; create and present a birthday card, self-portrait or greeting in the target language.
wider: Create and perform an original short play or role-play — not based on a modelled script — using known language for a new scenario
Present a created text to a real audience (another class, family members, school community) and adapt the presentation for that audience

response_modes.reason: Performance and presentation integrates written production (node 1) and purposeful text creation (node 2) into a full communicative act. The teaching investment is in creating real or realistic audience conditions — students performing for peers, younger students or family — that give the communication genuine stakes.

success_criteria: Performs or presents a created text using at least four target language phrases appropriate to the context
Demonstrates awareness of audience through manner of delivery — for example, appropriate volume, pace or expression
